$description: The register of locales that actually ship. This file is the single source of truth: the language menu is built from it at runtime, so a language cannot be offered unless its file is declared here, and a declared file that 404s demotes the locale rather than breaking the page. Key counts below are checked by tools/i18n-audit.mjs against the live DOM. Absent keys must be declared either as `superseded` (a translation withdrawn because the English it rendered no longer describes the site) or as `pending_translation` (a new string no translator has reached yet).
$fallback: Any key absent from a locale falls back to the English original held in memory from the source DOM. Fallen-back elements are marked data-i18n-fallback so the gap is visible rather than silent, and the count is reported on the i18n:applied event.
$offline: Not implemented. There is no service worker and no offline cache. The first switch to a language fetches its JSON over the network; subsequent switches within the same page view are served from an in-memory cache. English never needs a request because it is snapshotted from the DOM.

$data_coverage: 21 Oct 2026 (audit item 21). `complete` describes the brief's strings; `data_coverage` describes the records. "brief" means the brief is translated but the data overlay (i18n/<code>/data.json, about 5 KB against about 830 KB of records) covers only the Part I comparison table and calendar dates and obligations, so the observatory, the calendar's other fields and the instrument and tool pages stay largely in English. The language menu says so beside the language, so a reader choosing it is told before the page is not.
$edition: 22 Oct 2026 (audit items 20 and 22). `edition` is the locale's pre-rendered brief: `path` is its address below the site root, generated by tools/_footer.mjs from index.html and the locale's strings (tools/editions.mjs); `title` and `description` are its translated head, reviewed like every other string. Whether search engines are told about it is DERIVED from i18n/review/<code>.json: only a locale every string of which a person has approved, as it now stands, is indexable and gets hreflang (docs/SEO-OPERATIONS.md §6). Nothing here says a locale is reviewed; that is computed.
